neighbours.label: a component that limits or degrades a system's throughput (bottleneck, introduces latency/noise)
fire: The single disk controller quickly became a bottleneck once more users logged in.
In this pipeline the slow parser acts as a bottleneck for every downstream stage.
Each extra hop in the network introduces delay and reduces overall throughput.
The narrow bridge is a bottleneck that backs up traffic for miles every morning.
A cheap cable often introduces hum and noise into an otherwise clean recording.
Memory bandwidth, not compute, is the real bottleneck for this kind of model.
The manual approval step throttles the whole release process to one deploy per week.
Under heavy load the shared lock turns into a bottleneck that stalls all threads.
quiet: The single disk controller handled the load easily once more users logged in.
In this pipeline the fast parser feeds every downstream stage in turn.
Each extra server in the network adds capacity for more users.
The wide bridge carries traffic across the river every morning.
A good cable carries the signal cleanly into the recording interface.
Memory bandwidth and compute are both plentiful on this kind of machine.
The automated approval step lets the team deploy several times a day.
Under heavy load the shared cache keeps all threads running smoothly.

notes: Top peak ' bottleneck' (x2) then ' introduces' noise, 'first step ... that', ' activation', ' pedal'. Probe: 'became a bottleneck' 0.25 and 'introduces latency' 0.23, so the median may sit near the 0.20 bar.
